title: Concise reassurance and validation guide: regional relevance degradation
body:
SITUATION SUMMARY

Short summary (for status page and customer emails):
We observed a regional relevance degradation affecting embeddings-based search and similarity endpoints in EU-West between 2029-04-01 22:10 UTC and 2029-04-02 03:42 UTC. A subset of requests returned stale or lower-quality embeddings, causing increased mismatch rates for retrieval and reranking in affected tenants. No data loss or unauthorized access was detected.

This doc:
- Draft status-page update language
- Customer-facing post-incident recap and verification kit
- Suggested self-serve validation steps for integrators
- Proposed customer remediation/compensation wording (draft)

INTENDED AUDIENCE
Primary: engineering/product owners at affected customers, partner integrators, and internal CS leads. Secondary: account execs and SREs coordinating follow-up.

STATUS PAGE / SHORT UPDATE (45–60 word):
"We experienced a regional degradation impacting embedding similarity in EU-West from ~22:10 UTC (04/01) to ~03:42 UTC (04/02). This affected relevance for some customers’ retrieval and reranking flows. The issue is resolved and verified; detailed postmortem and validation steps are being published. If you saw anomalies, follow the verification steps or contact support."

DETAILED CUSTOMER-FACING POSTMORTEM (draft)
1) What happened (plain language)
- At 22:10 UTC on 2029-04-01, our telemetry began showing divergence in embedding vectors generated by our EU-West inference tier for a fraction of requests.
- Between 22:10 and 03:42 UTC, some embedding responses contained stale KV-cache entries from a transient cache-priming regression introduced in a deployment candidate (safe-telemetry branch) that was accidentally promoted to the EU-West pool.
- Result: similarity scores for downstream retrieval/rerank pipelines were degraded for impacted requests.

2) Customer impact (concise)
- Affected: Tenants routed to EU-West during the window; probability of experiencing degraded relevance varied by routing and request pattern.
- Not affected: Hosted completions, streaming tokens, and embeddings produced by non-EU-West regions.
- Data integrity: No embeddings were exfiltrated, and no user payloads were persisted outside normal retention policies.

3) Timeline (UTC)
- 2029-04-01 21:58 – Canary deploy initiated for safe-telemetry branch (internal note).
- 2029-04-01 22:10 – Alert: deviation in embedding distribution observed; first customer reports arrive.
- 2029-04-01 22:25 – Mitigation: traffic steering to fallback EU-Global pool applied for most tenants; partial rollback planned.
- 2029-04-02 00:05 – Rollback executed for EU-West pool to previous stable model runtime.
- 2029-04-02 01:20 – Validation run: sample tenants show improved vectors but some stale cache hits remain.
- 2029-04-02 03:10 – Completed cache flush and forced rebuild for affected nodes.
- 2029-04-02 03:42 – Final verification pass completed; metrics returned to baseline.
- 2029-04-02 09:00 – Customer success notified; this draft shared for review.

4) Root cause (technical summary for customers)
- A regression in cache-priming logic (introduced in safe-telemetry branch) caused KV-cache entries to be retained across model variant switches in EU-West. When a model runtime was briefly swapped during a canary promotion, some nodes served embeddings using stale cache state (older positional keys), producing vectors that were semantically shifted relative to expected outputs.
- The change passed unit tests and limited canary checks but did not trigger the specific distribution-shift detector we run for embedding vectors because the sample frequency was under-configured for EU-West traffic patterns.

5) Immediate remediation and verification (what we did)
- Immediately routed traffic away from EU-West to EU-Global fallback for high-risk tenants.
- Rolled back the safe-telemetry release and ran automated integrity checks.
- Performed full cache eviction on affected nodes and forced KV-cache rebuilds.
- Ran a 3-stage verification: (a) distribution alignment test vs. baseline, (b) downstream similarity regression checks on representative prompt set, (c) live tenant sanity sampling.
- Engaged with impacted customers via targeted emails and syncs.

6) Recommended self-serve validation steps (for engineering contacts)
- Quick smoke: request a known test embed and compare cosine similarity to expected baseline vector. Example curl (replace API_KEY and TENANT_ID):
  curl -sS -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings\" \\n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer API_KEY\" \\n    -H \"X-Tenant-ID: TENANT_ID\" \\n    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n    -d '{"input":"The Eiffel Tower in Paris"}'

- Compare cosine similarity to baseline (we will provide a small baseline set for affected tenants). If similarity drops > 0.12 relative to baseline for multiple samples, contact support.
- For retrieval pipelines: run 100 sample queries from your representative prompt set and compute top-k precision delta versus a snapshot we can provide.
- If you use dedicated routing or pinned model versions, verify your routing config in Console > Routing > Tenant.

7) Customer-facing verification kit we will provide (automated)
- CSV of 50 canonical query→ground-truth pairs and baseline embeddings (per affected tenant where available).
- A small Python script to compute cosine deltas and generate a short report.
- A support-run verification: we can run the suite against your tenant and share the report.

8) Longer-term fixes and guardrails
- Add distribution-shift monitors with higher sampling in regional pools and a targeted detector for embedding drift.
- Harden deployment gating to prevent cache-priming changes from hitting production without an explicit KV-cache-compatibility check.
- Expand canary sampling windows and add synthetic query traffic for embedding inspectors in low-volume regions.

9) Compensation and next steps (draft language for account teams)
We recognize the impact of degraded relevance and recommend offering affected customers a one-time credit proportional to time-on-impact and request volume. Proposed default: 10% of net usage in the impacted window for customers with >10k embedding units consumed in that window; otherwise, case-by-case. All credits to be processed after customer verification and acceptance.

10) Open questions / internal notes (to review before publishing)
- Decide final compensation threshold and sign-off owner (ops leadership).
- Confirm list of tenants actually routed through EU-West during window (data team to finalize).
- Agree final wording for public status page vs. personalized emails (legal review).
- Determine if we proactively rotate any tenant-specific keys as a precaution (security input).

11) Contact and escalation
- If you observed anomalies: please open a ticket at support@redwood.ai with subject prefix [INC-4821]. Include sample request IDs when possible.
- For urgent enterprise concerns, contact your CSM or escalate to enterprise-ops@redwood.ai.

12) Appendix: quick engineering glossary (plain terms)
- KV-cache: runtime cache used to store intermediate attention/position data to speed inference.
- Embedding drift: change in statistical distribution of embedding vectors resulting in lower similarity for the same inputs.
- Canary: a small release of new code to a subset of nodes to validate changes before wide rollout.

DRAFT NOTES:
- This file is a customer-facing draft; please add legal and privacy reviews before publishing.
- Action items for CS: confirm affected tenant list, prepare personalized verification kits for top 15 enterprise tenants, draft compensation letters.

END OF DRAFT

[notes to self: include brief troubleshooting sandbox link for customers and a small sample script in Python in a follow-up doc. Also follow up with eng team to create a short statuspage timeline visual we can attach to customer emails.]
